title: Structured Postpartum Support Protocol
implementation_guidance: Implement a structured postpartum support protocol that includes: 1) Scheduling at least three home visits within the first six weeks after birth; 2) Conducting systematic assessment of physical recovery, infant feeding, sleep patterns, and emotional wellbeing using validated screening tools; 3) Providing hands-on demonstration of infant care techniques including bathing, soothing methods, and safe sleep practices; 4) Offering evidence-based breastfeeding support with specific positioning guidance and troubleshooting for common challenges; 5) Screening for postpartum mood disorders using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale at each visit; and 6) Creating a personalized resource list for ongoing community support. The protocol should emphasize building parental confidence through positive reinforcement and practical skill development rather than taking over infant care tasks.
expected_outcomes: Increased breastfeeding duration and exclusivity, improved maternal confidence in infant care, earlier identification of postpartum mood disorders, reduced emergency department utilization for non-urgent infant concerns, and enhanced maternal-infant bonding.
target_population: All postpartum individuals, with particular emphasis on first-time parents, those with limited social support, and those at higher risk for postpartum mood disorders
citation: McLeish J, Redshaw M. A qualitative study of volunteer doulas working alongside midwives at births in England: Mothers' and doulas' experiences. Midwifery. 2018;56:53-60. doi:10.1016/j.midw.2017.10.002
